distractors.reason: We don't say 'wait at your turn'. 'Wait at' is used for places: wait at the bus stop.
We don't say 'wait on your turn'. 'Wait on' is an old-fashioned phrase meaning to serve people in a shop or restaurant.
We don't say 'wait to your turn'. 'Wait to' is used with an action: wait to play, wait to open the box.

example_sentence: Please wait ___ your turn to play with the new toy.
l1_interference: Po polsku mówi się 'czekać na' (np. czekać na kolej), więc uczniowie często wybierają 'on' albo 'to' zamiast 'for'. Poprawnie jest 'wait for'.
explanation: In English, 'wait for' is used when you stay in one place until someone or something comes, or until your turn arrives. Use 'for' after 'wait' with a person, a thing, or a time.

related_collocations.example: I like to listen to music when I play with my toys.
Look at this puzzle, it is very nice.

memory_tip: WAIT + FOR = stay until something comes (your turn, the bus, the game to start). WAIT + TO is not used for turns or waiting for people.
